requirements.requirement: node1 (OpenWrt) answers authoritative DNS for app.internal -> node2's IP (10.100.198.11) on the shared lan network
requirements.summary: A UCI dhcp.@domain record (app.internal -> 10.100.198.11) was added and committed, dnsmasq restarted, and confirmed listening on the shared br-lan address 10.100.198.10:53 (both TCP and UDP). A local nslookup on node1 resolves app.internal to 10.100.198.11. This configuration survived a full node1 reboot (baseline boot_id f90f49b2, changed to c5d4abec after restart) with dnsmasq status/config verified intact post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: node3 resolves app.internal via real DNS (pointed at node1) with no local /etc/hosts entry
requirements.summary: node3's NetworkManager connection was reconfigured to use 10.100.198.10 as DNS server (ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes), and /etc/resolv.conf reflects this. A grep of /etc/hosts for app.internal returns no match, while getent hosts and a Python socket.gethostbyname both resolve app.internal to 10.100.198.11, confirming resolution is via DNS rather than a static hosts entry. This held after node3's own reboot as well (resolv.conf and hosts-grep re-checked post-restart).

requirements.requirement: node3 can reach node2's HTTP service on port 8080 using the name app.internal
requirements.summary: curl to http://app.internal:8080/ from node3 returns HTTP 200 with node2's page content, both immediately after setup and after each node's subsequent reboot. Note: the task stated node2 already runs this service, but evidence shows it was not actually running at task start (ss/ps showed nothing on 8080); the executor created a systemd-managed python http.server and opened firewalld port 8080 to establish the real service being resolved/reached, which is a reasonable and necessary step to fulfill the stated end-to-end goal.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for node1: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id f90f49b2 and healthy dnsmasq/app.internal config captured pre-restart. First reboot attempt failed silently (nohup missing on OpenWrt ash) and was corrected with a working backgrounded reboot; ack issued, boot_id changed to c5d4abec after reconnection, and dnsmasq/app.internal resolution plus node3's end-to-end DNS+HTTP check were re-verified post-reboot. The fixed after_executor snapshot's boot-identity probe for node1 failed transiently (rc=255, likely timing/SSH), but other after_executor observations (differing uhttpd/dnsmasq PIDs) are consistent with the reboot the executor directly observed.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for node2: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 910dc564 and healthy service state captured. First reboot ack + boot_id change to a550fc49 confirmed, but the app-internal.service was found inactive post-boot due to a network-online.target dependency never satisfied on this image (a real bug). The unit was fixed to depend on network.target, restarted manually, then a second reboot was performed (boot_id changed to dfc3681f, cross-confirmed by the fixed after_executor snapshot) with the service automatically active and serving 200 without manual intervention.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for node3: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered DNS+HTTP state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 67c52137 and working DNS/HTTP state captured. Reboot ack issued, boot_id changed to aee30e7b (cross-confirmed by the fixed after_executor snapshot), and DNS resolution via 10.100.198.10 plus HTTP access to app.internal:8080 with no /etc/hosts entry were both re-verified post-reboot.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured node1's dnsmasq to authoritatively answer app.internal -> node2's IP over the shared lan interface, and configured node3 to use node1 as its DNS resolver with no /etc/hosts entry, then verified end-to-end name resolution and HTTP reachability to node2's port-8080 service. It also discovered that node2's stated HTTP service was not actually running and created a real one to allow genuine validation. All three nodes were taken through a full baseline/ack/changed-boot-id/recovery restart cycle, including catching and fixing a real systemd network-online.target boot-persistence bug on node2, with the fix validated by a second reboot.
limitations: The fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot's boot-identity probe for node1 returned an empty result (rc=255), likely a transient SSH/timing issue at collection time, so this specific cross-check for node1 relies on the executor's own final boot_id observation (c5d4abec) rather than the fixed snapshot.

The task premise stated node2 already runs the HTTP service, but evidence shows it did not exist before the executor created it; this is treated as a necessary prerequisite rather than an unrequested feature, but it is a deviation from the stated starting condition worth noting.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a material outcome: DNS config on node1, DNS override + verification on node3, the (necessary, since absent) HTTP service and firewall rule on node2, the three restart cycles, and the in-flight fix of node2's systemd unit dependency (a legitimate bug discovered during the mandated restart protocol). The one failed mutation attempt (cmd-2ac3dcf219b44ef1, a nohup reboot that errored because nohup is absent on OpenWrt ash) did not actually change state and was immediately corrected by cmd-e840ae075e6448e0, so it is not counted as residue. Post-executor temp-file diffs (systemd-private-* dirs, reboot.log) are normal reboot byproducts, not executor-created clutter. No abandoned files, conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare.
